blocks.md: **In 2015 the top 10% of US tax units received about half of all income, the top 1% about a fifth, and the top 0.1% about a tenth. New York and Florida top every list.**
State averages are lower (46.3%, 18.1%, 8.4%), because a few very unequal states pull the national figure up.

| Rank | Top 10% | Top 1% | Top 0.1% |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Florida 61.5% | New York 32.9% | New York 18.3% |
| 2 | New York 60.5% | Florida 30.4% | Florida 16.4% |
| 3 | Nevada 55.7% | Connecticut 28.4% | Wyoming 15.5% |
| 4 | Connecticut 55.2% | Nevada 26.4% | Nevada 15.2% |
| 5 | Massachusetts 54.4% | Massachusetts 25.6% | Connecticut 15.0% |
| 6 | California 54.0% | California 25.5% | Massachusetts 13.1% |

- Thresholds vary a lot: entering the top 1% takes \$671k in Connecticut but \$359k in Nevada.
- Wyoming ranks 7th for the top 1% and 3rd for the top 0.1%, despite being absent from the top-10% list — top shares measure the very top, not the overall shape.
